title: Timed/delayed suspend and shutdown feature
line: Right-clicking a Shut Down, Restart, Log Out, Sleep or Hibernate button in the Lock/Logout widget now lets you run it after 15 minutes to 2 hours, with a way to cancel.
explanation: The Lock/Logout widget could only run its actions immediately, so a delayed shutdown or sleep needed a terminal or the Timer widget's command. The widget now adds "<Action> in 15 Minutes / 30 Minutes / 1 Hour / 2 Hours" entries to the right-click menu of the button under the pointer (shut down, restart, log out, sleep, hibernate), plus "Cancel <Action> at <time>" while one is pending. A scheduled button gets a small clock badge and its tooltip says "Scheduled for <time>"; when the time comes it runs the same call as a click, so shutdown, restart and logout still go through the normal logout screen countdown.

commits.message:
applets/lock_logout: offer to run actions after a delay

Shutting down or sleeping after a delay needed a terminal or the Timer
widget. Right-clicking a button now offers to run it after 15 minutes to
2 hours, and a badge, the tooltip and a Cancel entry show the schedule.

BUG: 369845

media.caption: Master: right-clicking the Shut Down button only offers the standard widget entries.
Patched: the same menu offers Shut Down in 15 Minutes, 30 Minutes, 1 Hour or 2 Hours.
Master: the Shut Down button and its tooltip.
Patched, after picking 15 minutes: a clock badge on the button and the tooltip says Scheduled for 10:53 PM.
Patched: right-clicking another button (Sleep) offers its own delays and cancelling the pending shutdown.
Patched: at 10:53 PM the widget starts the shutdown and the logout screen counts down as usual (cancelled here).
